title: Turbulent channel flow validation vs KMM1987 DNS (Re_tau=180)
summary: SST reproduces the mean velocity u+(y+) of the imported low-Re channel DNS over the literal anchor window y+ in [30, centreline] with 3.46 % RMS relative error at 256 cells, but 6.12 % over the physical log layer y+ in [30, 0.2 Re_tau] = [30, 36.4]; the 5 % criterion therefore holds only under the legacy (diluted) window. k-omega and k-epsilon fail both windows (10.6 % / 6.8 % legacy). See grading_windows for both numbers.
dns_proxy: Lee & Moser 2015 JFM 774:395 (Re_tau=182.088). Substitution cost measured, not assumed: re-solving at the nominal Re_tau=180 changes the graded RMS by <0.02 percentage points and flips no verdict (see docs/verification-channel-kmm180-loglaw/REPORT.md section 3.3).
method: 1-D equilibrium channel solver with SST/k-omega/k-epsilon turbulence models
verdict: QUALIFIED: PASS under the legacy window y+ in [30, centreline]; FAIL under the physical log layer y+ in [30, 0.2 Re_tau]. Both numbers are published below and neither may be quoted alone.

legacy_full.definition: y+ in [30, centreline (180.56 at Re_tau=182.088)]; the literal reading of the anchor text
legacy_full.caveat: an outer-layer denominator (mean u+ 18.4 vs 16.3 in the log layer) dilutes a near-constant u+ offset; this window can pass without the log layer being reproduced

log_layer.caveat: at Re_tau=182 the physical log layer is only ~6 wall units wide, so this window is itself a compromise; the DNS deviates 3.04 % from the classic log law (kappa=0.41, B=5.2) over the same interval

acceptance_criterion: RMS relative deviation of u+(y+) in y+>30 region < 5%

critique.is_the_failure_a_solver_defect: No. Three independent checks. (a) Momentum identity: with unit friction velocity the equilibrium shear balance implies dU+/dln y+ = y+(1 - y/h)/(1 + nu_t+/nu), so the profile's log slope is predicted by the turbulence state alone; measured vs predicted kappa agrees to 0.029 % (SST) and 0.001 % (k-omega), i.e. no momentum-flux bookkeeping error -- the u+ deficit is carried entirely by nu_t. (b) At Re_tau=182 the state sits at kappa_eddy = nu_t+/y+ = 0.204 (SST) against the model's own closed-form kappa = 0.408; both k+ and kappa_eddy rise monotonically towards the closed-form values as Re_tau grows (k+ 2.67 -> 2.97 against 1/sqrt(beta*) = 3.333 from Re_tau 550 to 5200, kappa_eddy 0.285 -> 0.342 against 0.408). (c) Predicting k+ with the window-mean total-stress factor (1 - y/h) leaves a residual falling from 9.4 % to 3.3 %: the shortfall is the finite-domain (1 - y/h) factor plus a non-asymptotic y+=30, not bookkeeping.
critique.reference_substitution_bound: Measured, not assumed: re-solving at the nominal Re_tau=180 instead of the reference 182.088 changes the graded RMS by 0.02 pp (log layer) and 0.00 pp (legacy) and flips no verdict for sst or k-omega; Cf and U_bulk+ move by 0.43 % and 0.22 %.

test_cmd: PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/test_channel_kmm180_loglaw.py tests/test_channel_kmm180_windows.py tests/test_channel_kmm1987.py -q  # 41 passed
notes: k-omega and k-epsilon have known biases in the log region; SST is the best of the three models at this Re_tau but still misses the physical log layer. The reference is a documented proxy (KMM1987 -> Lee & Moser 2015); the substitution cost is bounded at <0.02 pp and is recorded rather than asserted.
